column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3a, to the judge only: Taiwan's highest court graded pension promises by whose money pays them (Interpretation 782, 2019), the line IPS l.11's anybody else's money draws; said as a parallel (a ruling on public pensions that ranks protection, not one that says budget-paid promises fail); carry row 2's quote here; never says what a co-sponsor reads.

Tue 17 Nov: the cut touched only the budget-paid part (782's reasoning); its quote rides in row 1; the use mis-maps the parallel: the court's split is own money against the budget's, i.e. l.11's anybody else's money, not l.11's Treasuries-for-promises against shares-for-unpromised split.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3d background: Taiwan's final payment guarantee was read as guaranteeing adjusted benefits; drop never guaranteed alone (a certainty guard Book 19 voids: Treasuries may be called guaranteed); keep name the instrument and dates, never secured, never liken her Treasuries to a Taiwanese government guarantee; in a Taiwanese ear is an inference with no source, say so.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: a dissent, not the holding; its use (why a Taiwanese reader hears guaranteed with care) would rebuild a certainty guard Book 19 voids and rests on no reader source; if used at all, only as the contrast that a guarantee of adjusted payments is not a debt of a stated amount on a stated date.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a background or store: spot-checked at source (781 reasoning: 18% fixed 1983 at a 7.55% one-year rate, then 2.95%, 1.16%, 1.07%); a fixed rate paid by a third party grew costlier as rates fell, the same falling rates the extra Treasuries guard the reinvested interest against; a designed subsidy, not an investment.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: sizes of the 18% bill (the NT$68.7bn total is Keel arithmetic on annex figures as quoted); 3a's density cut leaves no room for a Taiwan dollar figure, so it serves no part.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3a context: the floor part kept its 18% in the deepest cut; the bottom never moves after January 2028 is in NUMBERS section 3 (l.324, A variant Keel did not adopt), not a section 4 note, so cite it there; Taiwan's floor still rests on the next vote.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3a context: the payer set the speed of the cut (six-year draft, two and a half years enacted); the draft's yearly steps read in excerpt only; nothing in the ten waits on anyone's calendar but the bonds' own.

Tue 17 Nov: store fact only: year-11 return of principal (781 summary confirms); drop the conceit use: pencil and ink are defined for figures Laura's own Treasuries pay, CONCEIT V2.4 takes verified craft facts only, and 3a's one turn is already the interest on cash waiting; their principal sat in a state bank at a state-set rate.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, the strongest Taiwan contrast to IPS l.11, but fix two things: read at source, the 1979 report recommended starting at 5-7% (contributions actually began at 8% in 1995, 12% from 2006, against later break-even rates of 15.5-42.65%), so never began at 5-7%; and Laura was born in Wuhan and raised in Texas (case l.13), so never Laura's own country, say the country where her residency will run.

Tue 17 Nov: with row 10 in 3a or its note: read at source, 2.44% is the 2007-2016 average and the return needed at a 12% rate, including paying off past underfunding, was 10.6% for civil servants (782) and 27.7% for the military (781); give both or the civil-service 10.6%, never 27.7% alone as Taiwan's public pension fund.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d background: run-out dates and the reform's extension; a co-sponsor having lived with funds that will run out is Keel's inference (co-sponsors are firms, foundations and public bodies whose views no source records), so say so; SKELETON 3d already opens with the ten years owned.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: the rescue was more budget money (NT$100bn over ten years); nothing is owed that is not already owned holds from January 2028, when the top-up finishes the ten, not from January 2027.

Tue 17 Nov: store, evidence behind Q9c's 3d half-clause (one half-clause, no number, never a second clause): say how Taiwan's civil-service pensions ran until 1995, not how public promises have always run; ten owned years being rare there rests on Q9c, not on this row.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3e context in words: the 12 Dec 2025 reversal (52-50) shows public promises move with votes both ways; it raised payments, so instability, not loss; the court has not ruled (latest read 6 Aug 2026); sits beside card Q92's elections clause, never as a forecast of any party.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, one clause at most: Taiwan's Ministry of Civil Service called a budget top-up a bill shifted onto taxpayers not in the fund, the same idea as l.11's anybody else's money; always attributed to the ministry, which opposed the bill, never as a neutral finding.
Tue 17 Nov: guard row for rows 15-16: say three to four years earlier, never a run-out year (2045/2042 against 2045 to 2041 in the sources).

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3a context only: back pay waits on a pending ruling; drop the conceit use (pencil is defined for figures Laura's Treasuries pay, and 3a's one turn is taken); re-read the court's status at source before any use, since nothing after 6 Aug 2026 was checked.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3e: one strong year (15.96% in 2025) does not make a dated promise safe, the ministry's own words; secondary (a fact-check quoting officials); fits IPS l.15 (shares set the top and her flexibility) and Wharton's rule that WInS gains are never evidence.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a with rows 22-23: the labour pension floor is written on the national treasury (art. 23, official English read at source); drop every Taiwanese worker knows (no source); a floor on returns over a working life, not a dated payment.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3e: the labour floor is tested once, cumulatively, at withdrawal; Laura's bottom is measured once at purchase (NUMBERS section 3 l.324, not a section 4 note) by what she holds, not by a promise to top up.

Tue 17 Nov: store, with row 23: 8 of 21 years under the guaranteed rate (2005 a half year) yet NT$2.76tn earned against NT$427bn guaranteed (6.5 times, Keel arithmetic); a floor missed in a year is not a floor paid.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, claim 2's correction: the labour pension's treasury floor has never drawn on the budget (LY Budget Center 2016, 2020); drop best-known (no source), say the labour pension's; untested is not broken, and row 36 must travel with it so no judge reads Laura's Treasuries as an untested guarantee.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: after 2018 both labour funds had nothing to make up, buffers being earlier surplus; excerpt only, 2022 not checked.
Tue 17 Nov: the old-system fund carries the same clause (LSA art. 56) and missed its rate in 11 of 39 periods (Keel arithmetic); support for row 23, adds no new idea.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a background: the one Taiwan floor the treasury did pay took instalments from 2010 to 2017, someone else's money on someone else's schedule; strike also why IPS l.15 keeps half the shares (the IPS gives its own reasons; say a parallel to l.15's a co-sponsor falling short, never its cause); it was paid in full in the end.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d background: Labour Insurance top-ups (NT$387bn by 2025) buy years; a Taiwanese co-sponsor reads the government will cover it as this year's budget is Keel's inference with no reader source, so say so or drop it; the money did arrive each year.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, or the team's lead-in to 3d: the 2026 Labor Insurance Act makes the state ultimately responsible yet sizes each top-up by the year's finances, against Laura's size already owned; never in Laura's own words to co-sponsors, which comment on no government's promises.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, client knowledge with an aha: since 2015 Taiwan's law makes an employer hold next year's pensions in full by March; fix holds all ten years from January 2027 (most of each payment is bought January 2027 and the top-up, $2,388 at today's rates per NUMBERS, finishes them in January 2028); a parallel only, never that the law binds Laura or the residency (case l.169 puts Taiwan law out of scope); for 3d it must beat Q9c's residency clause, which it is further from.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a with row 29: factory closures left pensions unpaid, as the ministry's 2022 brief tells it (cases not read separately); say the law's fix parallels the plan (one year by law against ten by choice), never is the plan's design; a remembered cost is an inference about public memory, say so.

Tue 17 Nov: store only: in 2016 five of six special municipalities were short under the one-year rule, compliance 99.8% by 2022; never imply today's public co-sponsors are unreliable, and never in 3d, whose words never question a co-sponsor.

Tue 17 Nov: the lump-sum rule is row 29's detail; the 2023 judgment was not read (via the ministry's release); the plan does not buy each payment as a whole bond (iBond funds and rungs plus reinvested interest), so say each payment has its own Treasury maturing before it.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3a context: the 2005 labour pension moved money from an employer's promise to an account held for the worker; fix not promised by anyone: the ten are owed to her by the US Treasury, held for her, not promised by a co-sponsor; the account still sits in a state-run pooled fund.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: the farmers' fund carries the same treasury floor and lost 3.78% in 2022 against 1.10%; a Taiwanese reader expects a stated floor is an inference with no source, drop it.

Tue 17 Nov: guard for 3a and 3d: co-sponsors never see the IPS, so what they read first in l.11 is at most Keel's inference, and the row says so; the verified events allow only that l.11's line is the one Taiwan's court drew, while 3d opens with the ten years owned as SKELETON already orders.

Tue 17 Nov: travels with any use of this card: Taiwan's promises were statutory and changed by vote, Laura's ten are Treasuries owed to her; l.11's anybody else's money means co-sponsors', donors' or third parties' money; Treasuries may be called guaranteed (Book 19), never the government's guarantee in the Taiwanese pension sense; a US default said once, in 3e.
